title: Concise Migration Cheat Sheet and Auditable Changelog Template for LTS/Canary Upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, customer-facing migration cheat sheet and a machine-auditable changelog template that can be used for LTS channels and canary rollouts. The deliverable should be a set of copy-ready comms (email, in-console banner, support KB) plus a structured changelog format that maps to our rollout gates and upgrade tooling (automated canary flags, forced fallback triggers, and rollback hooks). The goal is to reduce customer confusion during staged rollouts, make upgrade impact transparent, and provide a single source of truth for support and account teams.
objective: Ensure all customers on LTS and dedicated deployments receive clear, action-oriented upgrade guidance tied to rollout gates and rollback procedures; provide a changelog schema that can be parsed by internal dashboards and the Console's release timeline UI.
migration_checklist: Inventory affected endpoints and recommended model versions
Document config changes required (batching/quantization defaults) per tier
List pre-upgrade validation queries and expected outputs
Confirm backup windows and snapshot cadence for Dedicated/Private customers
Verify canary cohort definitions and health metrics for gating
changelog_template:
Format: [version] | [channel:LTS|Canary|GA] | [date] | [semantic impact: none|minor|breaking] | [summary] | [migration_footnotes]
Notes: 'migration_footnotes' should include explicit 'actions required' or 'auto-upgrade' flags. Attach 'rollback_commands' and 'observability-links' fields for operator consumption.
comms_timeline: T-21d: Publish short 'heads up' to admin contacts with high-level impact and timeline
T-10d: Release detailed migration guide and changelog (includes pre-checklist and expected perf delta)
T-3d: In-product banner for affected customers with direct link to KB and scheduled upgrade window
Day-0 (canary start): Send canary cohort notification; include feedback form link and incident contact
Day+1 (canary review): Share preliminary canary health summary with all customers and support teams
Day+7 (progressive rollout): Notify next cohort and reiterate rollback conditions and support hours
Post-rollout: Publish final changelog entry and migration acceptance checklist
audience_segments: Self-serve hosted API customers with active usage in last 90 days
communication_templates: Short admin email (subject): Upcoming runtime-1.20 LTS maintenance and optional migration steps - body: 3 bullet summary, upgrade window, action required flag, link to guide, support SLA contact.
Detailed changelog excerpt (markdown): Includes version header, semantic impact, migration_footnotes with code snippets for client SDK pinning and rollout gate opt-outs.
In-console banner copy: One-sentence impact line, 'Learn more' CTA to migration KB, 'Remind me' button to schedule a check-in with Solutions.
Support KB template: Problem statement, why it changed, CLI/SDK commands to validate, mitigation steps, rollback commands, sample support logs to attach to a ticket.
Account communication (CSM/AM): Suggested talking points, risk assessment matrix, recommended migration schedule tailored by customer size and SLA tier.
rollback_plan: Define two rollback paths: automated (fast) and manual (safe). Automated rollback triggers: canary error rate > 5% OR latency P95 degradation > 2x for 10m window -> auto-fallback to previous model variant. Manual rollback: support-run upgrade revert using 'redwood upgrade revert --release <version>' with pre-approved maintenance window. Document post-rollback postmortem steps and customer notification cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Comms templates reviewed by 2 PMs and 1 design reviewer
Changelog schema validated by runtime and console teams and ingests cleanly into release-ui staging
Migration checklist and KB published in Confluence/Drive and linked from Console
Support runbook outlining triage steps and rollback commands is published and acknowledged by Oncall rotation
Pilot canary cohort notification executed and monitored; health report captured
